title: Leaving what your Lord made for you.
subtitle: Transgression is walking past the lawful
then: Lut {idea}taught them to turn to the wives Allah had created for them.{/idea} The lawful was already provided and close at hand. He calls them {trap}a trespassing people{/trap}: they went past what was given to reach what was forbidden.
now: Your spouse is in the next room while you scroll toward something you should not. Your salary is enough, and you still reach for what is not yours. {idea}The lawful was already provided.{/idea}
old: I cross limits because what is allowed does not satisfy me.
new: Allah already placed what is good for me within reach; transgressing is walking past it.
try: Spend real attention today on one lawful blessing you usually overlook, like your spouse or your family.

title: Stop, Lut, or we will drive you out.
subtitle: When people want to be clean, the town expels them
then: Their response was only: {trap}if you do not give up what you have brought, we will expel you from among us.{/trap} Elsewhere they said, {idea}they are people who want to be clean and pure.{/idea} His purity was their complaint.
now: You stop joining the gossip at work, or stop drinking at the team dinner. Slowly, the invitations stop. {idea}Sometimes being left out is a sign you are on the right side.{/idea}
old: If people push me out, I must be doing something wrong.
new: Being pushed out for doing right is a cost the messengers paid too.
try: If you have lost a circle for doing right, thank Allah for the reason, and seek better company.

title: I detest what you do.
subtitle: Lut declares himself free of their deed
then: When Lut saw {trap}they would not give up their ways{/trap}, he said he was among those who detest {idea}their deed.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}I do not like it, I do not accept it, I have nothing to do with it.{/idea}
now: Your friends joke about something cruel, and you laugh along so you do not seem uptight. Silence and laughter both sound like approval. {idea}You can refuse the deed without hating the person.{/idea}
old: If I stay friendly, I have to accept what they do.
new: I can stay kind to people while clearly refusing their wrong.
try: Next time a cruel joke comes up today, do not laugh. Calmly change the subject.

title: My Lord, save me and my family.
subtitle: A prayer for protection from surrounding harm
then: After declaring himself free of their deed, Lut {idea}prayed to Allah{/idea}: save me and my family from what they do. He was one man with his household, surrounded by a whole town. {reward}He turned the problem over to his Lord.{/reward}
now: You worry about what your kids see on their phones, at school, in the street. You cannot control all of it. {idea}You can make Lut's dua for them every night.{/idea}
old: Protecting my family depends entirely on me.
new: I do my part, and I ask the One who can actually protect them.
try: Tonight, make dua by name for each person in your household to be kept safe from harm.

title: So We saved him and his family.
subtitle: The dua was answered
then: Allah answered: {reward}We saved him and his family.{/reward} Allah commanded him to leave with his family at night and {idea}not to turn around{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes {reward}they patiently obeyed the command of Allah and persevered.{/reward}
now: You need to leave something behind: a job that pulls you into wrong, a circle that drags you down. Leaving is the first step. {idea}Not turning back to it is the second.{/idea}
old: Once I pray, the rescue should just happen to me.
new: Rescue often comes as a command to walk out, and patience not to look back.
try: If there is something you have already left for Allah, take one step today to not go back to it.

title: Except one who stayed behind, his own wife.
subtitle: Being close to a prophet was not enough
then: Ibn Kathir says this was {trap}his wife, who was a bad old woman{/trap}. She stayed behind and met the fate of those who remained. She lived inside a prophet's house, and {idea}it did not save her.{/idea}
now: Your father is the imam, your mother never misses a prayer, your brother memorized the Quran. It is easy to feel covered by them. {idea}Their closeness to Allah is theirs.{/idea}
old: Coming from a religious family keeps me safe.
new: No one's faith can carry me; I have to choose my own.
try: Do one act of worship today purely as your own, not because family expects it.

title: Then the rest were destroyed.
subtitle: After the believers left
then: The word {idea}then{/idea} matters. Lut and his family were brought out first. {trap}Afterward, the others were destroyed.{/trap} Allah separated those who obeyed from those who stayed.
now: When things fall apart around you, a company scandal, a friend group collapsing, it can feel random. {idea}The question is where you were standing before it came.{/idea}
old: When disaster comes, it does not matter what I did.
new: What I choose before the test decides where I stand in it.
try: Ask yourself honestly where you are standing today. Take one step to the side you want to be on.

title: A rain on those who had been warned.
subtitle: The weight is in the word warned
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {trap}rained upon them stones of baked clay, piled up.{/trap} The verse names them by one quality: {idea}those who had been warned.{/idea} Lut had told them plainly, and they had threatened him in return.
now: The doctor told you about your blood sugar. Your boss told you about the deadlines. Your heart told you about that habit. {idea}You were warned. That is a mercy while there is still time.{/idea}
old: Bad outcomes just come out of nowhere.
new: Most warnings come early; what I do with them is mine.
try: Take one warning you have been given, health, money or faith, and act on it today.

title: A sign left in the land itself.
subtitle: The refrain after Lut's story
then: Ibn Kathir notes the land of Lut's people became a lake {idea}well known in the land of Al-Ghur, the Jordan Valley.{/idea} Travelers passed it. The refrain repeats: {trap}in this is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.{/trap}
now: You drive past the hospital, the cemetery, the house of the neighbor who lost everything. You have seen it so often it means nothing now. {idea}A sign can become scenery.{/idea}
old: I have seen enough reminders to know them already.
new: The danger is not missing the sign, but getting used to it.
try: Next time you pass a place that reminds you of death or loss, stop for a moment and reflect.

title: Mighty against the town, merciful to one family.
subtitle: Both names seen in Lut's story
then: A mighty nation was ended, and one small family walked out at night. {idea}His might was not stopped by their numbers.{/idea} {reward}His mercy found the few who obeyed.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ and his small group in Makkah heard this.
now: You feel outnumbered: the only one in your office who prays, the only one in your family trying to change. {reward}Allah's mercy does not need a crowd.{/reward}
old: If most people are doing it, I am probably safe going along.
new: Allah sees the one who obeys, even alone among many.
try: Do one right thing today that you would normally skip because no one around you does it.

title: The people of the thicket denied too.
subtitle: Madyan, named after what they worshipped
then: The companions of Al-Aykah were, by the most correct view, {idea}the people of Madyan.{/idea} They took their name from Al-Aykah, {trap}a tree, or a thicket of tangled trees, which they used to worship.{/trap} They too denied the messengers.
now: People are often known by what they chase: the gym guy, the crypto guy, the one always talking about her career. {idea}What would you be named after?{/idea}
old: What I am obsessed with is just a hobby.
new: What I give my heart to can become my identity.
try: Ask a close friend what you talk about most. Listen to the answer honestly.

title: Shu'ayb spoke, but not called their brother.
subtitle: A missing word that tells a story

row.title: their name
sub: tied to the tree they worshipped

row.title: he was not one of them
the name was the tree's
sub: he shared their blood, not that

then: Here the Quran says {idea}when Shu'ayb said to them{/idea}, not their brother Shu'ayb. Ibn Kathir explains it is because {trap}their name denoted their worship of Al-Aykah.{/trap} Shu'ayb was their brother by blood but had no share in that name.
now: You can belong to a family, a team, a culture, and still not share in what is wrong in it. {idea}Belonging does not mean taking the whole label.{/idea}
old: If I belong to a group, I have to carry everything it stands for.
new: I can be loyal to my people without sharing in what they worship besides Allah.
try: Think of one thing your circle takes for granted that you do not agree with. Keep your distance from it, kindly.

title: A trustworthy messenger to a dishonest market.
subtitle: Shu'ayb's honesty set against their cheating
then: Shu'ayb says {reward}I am a trustworthy messenger to you.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes he {idea}commanded them to be fair in weights and measures.{/idea} A people who cheated in trade were sent a man defined by trust.
now: You sell a used phone and do not mention the cracked camera. You file an expense that is a bit rounded up. {idea}Trustworthiness is tested at the till, not only at the mosque.{/idea}
old: Business is business; faith is separate.
new: Being trustworthy covers my receipts as much as my prayers.
try: In your next sale or purchase, mention one detail that is in the other person's favor.

title: Fear Allah and obey me, said the fifth messenger.
subtitle: The same call reaches Madyan
then: Shu'ayb gives the same call as Nuh, Hud, Salih and Lut: {idea}have taqwa of Allah, and obey me.{/idea} For Madyan, obeying him would mean {reward}fair weights and measures{/reward}, right where they made their living.
now: Your shop, your freelance invoices, your online store. That is where your taqwa will be tested most this week. {idea}Mindfulness of Allah goes to work with you.{/idea}
old: I am mindful of Allah when I pray.
new: Mindfulness of Allah is just as real when I quote a price.
try: Before your next work task today, say bismillah and remember Allah is watching the work.

title: To traders, he asked no payment.
subtitle: Shu'ayb's call came free
then: To a people who lived by buying and selling, Shu'ayb said: {reward}no reward do I ask of you for it; my reward is only from the Lord of all the worlds.{/reward} He was the {idea}fifth messenger in this surah to say it.{/idea}
now: You are used to paying for everything: courses, coaching, advice. Then someone gives you honest guidance for free and you value it less. {idea}Free does not mean cheap.{/idea}
old: Advice I did not pay for cannot be worth much.
new: The most valuable guidance often comes from people asking nothing in return.
try: Thank someone today who once gave you good advice for free.
